newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, February 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, February 20.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories in the Irish press on Thursday.

- China's paramount leader, Deng Xiaoping, who transformed the world's most populous nation into an economic power died on Wednesday night at his home in Beijing of complications from Parkinson's Disease and a lung infection.
- The Irish government must urgently develop a strategy for dealing with any sharp fall in the value of sterling after monetary union, according to a National Economic and Social Council report.
- The SDLP has rebuffed renewed calls for an electoral pact, which Sinn Fein claims could result in the two parties winning eight Westminster seats.
- AIB is moving to take a majority shareholding in Wiekopolski Bank Kredytowy (WBK) of Poland at a cost of about 43 million Irish pounds.
- The Irish Central Bank should significantly reduce domestic interest rates, ISME, the Irish Small and Medium Enterprises Association has said.
- The last great emperor of Chinese Communism died on Wednesday, plunging the country into a grave political crisis.
- The Irish government may have to pay universities in Britain and the North to help solve a looming skills shortage in our computer industry.
- The Irish government is facing a bill of at least 180 million Irish pounds to compensate Hepatitis C blood contamination scandal victims.
- The decision of Equality and Law Minister Mervyn Taylor to step down at the next general election has further dented Labour's chances of getting anywhere near the 33 seats it achieved in 1992.
- The Dublin stock exchange reached a new high on Wednesday at 3,021.74 as equity markets around the world responded positively to the prospect of no increase in interest rates.
- Irish police swoops on suspected IRA haunts in different parts of the country are set to intensify over the coming days after the significant seizures of vital bomb components.

- Irish opposition Fianna Fail member Brian Crowley told nurses balloting on strike action to reject the government's pay deal, insisting the threat of industrial action would force the Health Minister, Michael Noonan into upping his offer.
- The European Parliament on Wednesday condemned Britain and the European Commission for mismanaging the BSE crisis.
- The theft of components from the burgeoning computer industry has turned into a multi-million pound international industry which offers profits akin to that involved in drug trafficking.
